## The claim

The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.

**Prediction if true.** D4 (TP53, MTOR, CDK4/6, IGF1R - broadly drugged cancer targets) overlaps at least one decoy's approved drug set at Jaccard >= 0.10; the decoy cards' automated rung distributions (approval, label, rhabdomyosarcoma trials) look like BUB1B's because the tumour-context queries are gene-independent.

**What would refute it.** Every direction's approved drug set has Jaccard < 0.10 against both decoy cards' approved sets - the automated pipeline alone already separates the mechanism from the decoys.

## Evidence

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 116 | supports | 0.80 | measurement | D4's 205 approved drugs overlap the NTRK3 decoy card's 171 at Jaccard 0.249 (75 shared), and all approved drugs at 0.269; D1-D3 stay below 0.10 against NTRK3 (0.064, 0.081, 0.023) and every direction stays below 0.10 against XDH (max 0.064). | `methodology/112` |
| 117 | supports | 0.60 | measurement | The trial-based automated rung is gene-independent by construction: 64 of NTRK3's and 8 of XDH's approved drugs have a rhabdomyosarcoma trial with the gene never consulted, and after the first grading run 85 BUB1B drugs sat at automated rung 5 on mechanism directions; the rule was refined so trial rungs grade the tumour-context direction alone. | `methodology/112` |
